france24fr.title: Ingérences russes en Arménie : un pays à l’épreuve de la désinformation

france24fr.title: Guinée–Mali : l’insécurité sur le corridor perturbe l’économie

Plus de 500 migrants sont actuellement accueillis dans des centres d'hébergement temporaire dans la province du Cap occidental.

observador.description: Entre 2015-2025, 64% dos indicadores relativos à saúde mostraram um progresso favorável. Na educação, 33,3% apresentaram evolução negativa, apesar das melhorias no acesso e na conclusão escolar.

observador.title: Custos energéticos: 600 milhões para empresas afetadas
observador.description: A Linha Portugal Resiliência Energética, destinada a apoiar empresas afetadas pelo aumento dos custos energéticos, fruto do conflito no Médio Oriente, será gerida pelo Banco Português de Fomento.

observador.title: Morreu ator britânico Anthony Head
observador.description: Carreira de Anthony Head ganhou dimensão internacional na década de 1990, pelo desempenho do bibliotecário Rupert Giles, na série Buffy, Caçadora de Vampiros, mentor da protagonista.

observador.title: Modelo de ação social: reitores apontam aspetos a clarificar
observador.description: O novo modelo de ação social prevê que o cálculo do valor das bolsas passará a considerar o custo médio de estudar no ensino superior e o rendimento que as famílias podem disponibilizar ao estudante.

observador.title: SATA reforça operação de verão com aluguer de avião Dash 400
observador.description: Companhia aérea informa que integrará para reforço da frota uma aeronave em regime de aluguer, com o objetivo de "garantir o cumprimento do programa de voos previsto para período de maior procura".

observador.title: Promulgado diploma para acelerar renováveis
observador.description: Entre as medidas previstas está a criação das Zonas de Aceleração da Implantação de Energia Renovável, onde os projetos beneficiam de procedimentos de licenciamento mais curtos e simplificados.

observador.title: Costa e Von der Leyen apoiam encontro entre Zelensky e Putin
observador.description: António Costa frisa que, desde o dia da invasão russa, a UE tem procurado ajudar a Ucrânia a chegar a uma "paz justa e duradoura". Von der Leyen assegura que a Ucrânia "tem o nosso apoio total".

observador.title: Seguro está alinhado com Governo sobre envelhecimento
observador.description: O primeiro-ministro defendeu que o Governo tem tido uma estratégia transversal para o envelhecimento que integra três aumentos significativos do Complemento Solidário para Idosos.

observador.title: Os hospitais tornaram-se o último refúgio para os idosos?
observador.description: Muitos portugueses ocupam camas de hospital por falta de resposta social. Polémica sobre onde colocar o chapéu de sol nas zonas concessionadas levanta a questão: as praias deixaram de ser para todos?

observador.title: As mensagens comprometedoras da mulher-sombra do PSOE
observador.description: Leire Díez é suspeita de ter agido nos bastidores para encontrar informações comprometedoras dos responsáveis pelos processos judiciais que cercam Sánchez. Caso gera forte pressão sobre o PSOE.

observador.title: Homem morre em acidente com trator agrícola em Resende
observador.description: A vítima estava a fazer a limpeza de terrenos quando o trator capotou. O óbito foi declarado no local pelo INEM, no concelho de Resende, distrito de Viseu.

observador.title: PSU. Chega exige limitação de apoios para imigrantes
observador.description: A estimativa do Chega é que 25 a 30% dos imigrantes recebam prestações sociais. Desde abonos a rendimentos sociais de inserção, o partido refere que são várias as prestações.

observador.title: Tromalyt, para doenças cardiovasculares, em rutura de stock
observador.description: "Medicamento Tromaly encontra-se em rutura de 'stock', por motivos de fabrico, até 31/07/2026", refere o Infarmed. Será temporariamente permitida a substituição, em prescrições já emitidas e válidas.

spiegel.title: Keir Starmer hält russischen Angriff auf Nato in vier Jahren für möglich
spiegel.description: Großbritanniens Premierminister Keir Starmer hat vor einem russischen Angriff auf die Nato in der Zukunft gewarnt. Das Land will deshalb stärker in Verteidigung investieren.

spiegel.title: Tom Schilling hält sein jugendliches Aussehen auch für einen Fluch
spiegel.description: Als Tom Schilling mit »Crazy« seinen Durchbruch feierte, kaufte ihm niemand ab, dass er 18 war. Nun hat er in einem Interview erzählt, wie ihn das den Schauspieler bis heute prägt.

spiegel.title: USA: Gericht erklärt Stopp von Einwanderungsanträgen für rechtswidrig
spiegel.description: Nach Schüssen auf zwei Nationalgardisten verschärft Präsident Trump die Einwanderungspolitik der USA. Unter anderem dürfen keine Greencards und Asylgesuche mehr bewilligt werden. Zu Unrecht, hat nun ein Richter geurteilt.

spiegel.title: Donald Trump plant offenbar Entlassungswelle bei US-Geheimdiensten
spiegel.description: Die Behörden des US-Geheimdienstes werden kleiner: Noch vor Amtsantritt des neuen Koordinators Bill Pulte hat Trump ihn einem Bericht zufolge angewiesen, eine große Zahl von Mitarbeitern zu entlassen.

spiegel.title: Wladimir Putin und Ex-Kanzler Gerhard Schröder führen Vieraugengespräch
spiegel.description: Gerhard Schröder und der russische Präsident Wladimir Putin sollen sich getroffen haben. Putin hatte den Ex-Kanzler zuvor als Vermittler im Ukrainekrieg vorgeschlagen.

spiegel.title: Leck an der Internationalen Raumstation ISS: Die Grenze zwischen Leben und Tod ist etwa so dick wie ein Geldstück
spiegel.description: Die ISS verliert ständig Luft. Nun hatte sich die Situation so zugespitzt, dass ein Teil der Crew in die Rettungskapsel beordert wurde. Das Problem betrifft eines der ältesten Module – und die Mülleimer der Astronauten.

spiegel.title: Mount Everest: Dawa Sherpa stürzte in Gletscherspalte, wurde von Lawine gerettet
spiegel.description: Ein Sherpa verliert Anschluss an seine Gruppe, kriecht Tage später zum Basecamp. Helfer berichten nun, was passiert sein soll: Demnach stieg er allein ab und fiel in eine Gletscherspalte. Eine Lawine rettete ihm das Leben.

spiegel.title: Angriff auf Frau: Hamburger Wolf ist laut Umweltbehörde wahrscheinlich tot
spiegel.description: Der Wolf, der vor gut zwei Monaten eine Frau in der Hamburger Innenstadt verletzt hat, ist vermutlich tot. Der Sender an dem freigelassenen Tier schickt offenbar keine Signale mehr.

spiegel.title: WM 2026: Lennart Karl verletzt – DFB-Hoffnung droht Turnieraus
spiegel.description: Vor dem letzten WM-Testspiel gegen die USA muss das DFB-Team einen schweren Rückschlag verkraften: Hoffnungsträger Lennart Karl fällt womöglich länger aus. Auch die Rückkehr von Manuel Neuer verzögert sich.

spiegel.title: ESC 2026: Finale in Wien hatte Millionen weniger Zuschauer
spiegel.description: Rund 131 Millionen Menschen sahen jüngst zu, wie Dara aus Bulgarien den Eurovision Song Contest »bangaranga« machte. Das klingt viel, ist aber deutlich weniger als im Vorjahr. Woran das liegt.

spiegel.title: Die Alpen brechen auf: Neue Gefahren am Berg – SPIEGEL TV für Arte Re:
spiegel.description: Der Klimawandel verändert die Alpen rasant: Schmelzende Gletscher und plötzliche Unwetter machen Bergtouren riskanter. Selbst erfahrene Bergsteiger müssen umdenken. Eine »Arte Re:«-Reportage von SPIEGEL TV.

spiegel.title: Verbrenner-Aus: Sieben EU-Länder erklären »ehrgeizigen Kurs« für E-Autos
spiegel.description: Mehrere Länder stellen sich gegen abgeschwächte EU-Regeln zum Verbrenner-Aus und planen einen strikten Kurs in Richtung E-Mobilität – mit einer klaren Ansage an Deutschland.

spiegel.title: Joko und Klaas und ihre Ukraine-Doku: Diese Sendung ist ein Stück TV-Geschichte
spiegel.description: Die TV-Unterhalter Joko und Klaas haben Sendezeit erspielt – und sie genutzt wie nie: Fünf Menschen filmen aus der Ego-Perspektive, was sie einen Tag lang in der Ukraine erleben. Ein roher Blick auf den Krieg, ohne Filter.

spiegel.title: »Eyes Full« von Zoh Amba: Manche Dämonen lassen sich nur mit Gitarrenlärm besiegen
spiegel.description: Zoh Amba war schon ein Jazzstar, dann entdeckte das Saxofontalent Gesang und Gitarre, um alte Kindheitstraumata zu bannen. Ambas Rockmusik-Debüt »Eyes Full« ist eine Sensation. Diese neuen Songs sollten Sie hören.

spiegel.title: Deutschland: Wie Staatsanwälte für ihre Unabhängigkeit streiten
spiegel.description: Staatsanwältinnen und Staatsanwälte sind in Deutschland politisch weisungsgebunden. Sie wollen, dass sich daran endlich etwas ändert. Eine Landesjustizministerin geht sogar noch weiter.

spiegel.title: Itamar Ben-Gvir, Bezalel Smotrich: Einreiseverbot von Irland für Israels Minister
spiegel.description: Spanien, Slowenien, Australien, Neuseeland, Norwegen, Großbritannien: Die Liste der Länder, die Sanktionen gegen Itamar Ben-Gvir und Bezalel Smotrich verhängen, ist lang. Nun untersagt auch Dublin ihnen die Einreise.

spiegel.title: A20 in Niedersachsen: Start der Bauarbeiten für umstrittene Moorautobahn
spiegel.description: Trotz des Sanierungsstaus bei alten Autobahnen, baut Deutschland sogar neue Trassen. Der Verkehrsminister hat gleich zwei Großbaustellen im Norden eröffnet. Jetzt wird auch kostbarer Moorboden asphaltiert.

spiegel.title: »Gothic«-Remake im Test: Was taugt die Neuauflage des Rollenspielklassikers?
spiegel.description: Das Rollenspiel »Gothic« hat auch ein Vierteljahrhundert nach Erscheinen viele Fans. Jetzt wurde das Kultspiel neu aufgelegt. Doch kann das Remake den Zauber von einst wieder aufleben lassen?

nyt.title: U.S. Job Market Pushes Past Shocks and Strains
nyt.description: Employers added 172,000 jobs in May, adding to a vigorous pace of hiring in recent months. But wage growth is not keeping up with higher prices and consumers remain pessimistic.

nyt.title: Stocks Slide as Investors See Rates Rising After Strong Jobs Data
nyt.description: The S&P 500 fell more than 2.6 percent on Friday, its worst one-day drop of the year and ending nine weeks of gains.

nyt.title: Central Ohio Becomes Hub for Tech and Manufacturing
nyt.description: Tech titans and Silicon Valley transplants changed the Columbus area, but not everyone is thrilled about the rapid transformation.

nyt.title: Trump Keeps Immunity from I.R.S. Audits, Even as $1.8 Billion Fund Falls Away
nyt.description: Even as they rebelled against a $1.8 billion fund for President Trump’s allies, Republicans looked the other way as his administration granted him potentially lucrative tax protections.

nyt.title: Graham Platner Controversy Deepens Democratic Unease Before Maine Senate Primary
nyt.description: The party’s politicians, officials and strategists wrestled with how to respond to new reporting about Graham Platner, with worries rising about his vulnerabilities in a general election.

nyt.title: Several Women Who Dated Graham Platner Recall ‘Unsettling’ Behavior
nyt.description: The Democratic candidate for Senate in Maine could be charming, women said in interviews, but some found his actions intimidating and disturbing.

nyt.title: Chuck Schumer Privately Backs Haley Stevens in Michigan Democratic Senate Primary
nyt.description: Chuck Schumer, the Democratic minority leader, has remained officially neutral on the race, but in conversations with donors, he has been clear about which candidate he supports.

nyt.title: Many Trump Voters Are Unhappy With Handling of Iran, Economy and More Issues
nyt.description: The president’s base is thought to be unmovable. But one-third of these voters say they are unhappy about certain issues and are not knee-jerk loyalists.

nyt.title: Why the SpaceX IPO Will Affect Your 401(k), Like It or Not
nyt.description: Elon Musk’s rocket company, on the cusp of the largest initial public offering ever, will soon end up in index funds after rule changes by Nasdaq and other index providers.

nyt.title: Elon Musk Dominates List of Highest Paid C.E.O.s
nyt.description: Executive compensation is accelerating while rank-and-file workers lag, widening the pay gap in corporate America.

nyt.title: 38 Tony Nominees Reveal the Strangest Skills They’ve Picked Up
nyt.description: The stars of “Giant,” “Fallen Angels,” “The Rocky Horror Show,” “Ragtime” and more prove they’ll go to great lengths to be believable in a role.

nyt.title: 2026 Tony Awards Predictions: Who Will Win?
nyt.description: Expect wins for the musical “Schmigadoon!” and the play “Liberation,” and for the “Ragtime” stars Joshua Henry and Caissie Levy.

nyt.title: First U.S. Screwworm Case Since 1960s Prompts Texas Emergency Response
nyt.description: After a screwworm infestation was confirmed in a South Texas calf, officials launched an aggressive effort to prevent the parasite from spreading in the nation’s largest cattle-producing state.

nyt.title: Man Who Schemed With Au Pair to Kill His Wife Is Sentenced to Life
nyt.description: Brendan Banfield was found guilty of murdering his wife and another man, who was lured in through a fetish website. The plan involved his lover, who is now serving 10 years in prison.

nyt.title: ’60 Minutes’ Stars Will Stay After Pelley’s Firing Because They Don’t Want Show to ‘Die’
nyt.description: Lesley Stahl, Bill Whitaker and Jon Wertheim said on Friday in an email to the show’s staff that they had reached the decision after a period of “grieving” and frustration.

nyt.title: ‘60 Minutes’ Turmoil: What to Know After Scott Pelley’s Firing
nyt.description: Scott Pelley’s firing is the latest in a string of controversies and staffing shake-ups that have plagued CBS’s news division.

nyt.title: From Cow-Milking Robots to Weed-Zapping Lasers, Farmers Are Embracing A.I.
nyt.description: We asked three farmers to tell us how new technology is revolutionizing the way they work.

nyt.title: What Are A.I. Agents Actually Doing?
nyt.description: A San Francisco start-up called Arena found that people are most likely to use A.I. agents on the job, particularly if they are in the tech industry.

republika.description: Si stringe il cerchio degli investigatori sul gruppo che ha aggredito e ucciso a coltellate il ventiduenne Gianluca Ibarra Silvera. Il fermato è un ragazzo di 19 anni accusato di omicidio aggravato

republika.title: Andrea Purgatori, quattro medici a processo per la morte del giornalista: “Omicidio colposo”
republika.description: Il professor Gianfranco Gualdi, tra i radiologi più conosciuti d’Italia, i suoi collaboratori Claudio Di Biasi e Maria Chiara Colaiacomo, e il cardiologo Guido Laudani dovranno presentarsi in aula il prossimo 12 gennaio

republika.title: Via alla festa di nozze per Dua Lipa e Callum Turner: piazza Croce dei Vespri come il set di un film
republika.description: Oggi il primo party nel centro storico di Palermo. Domani il bis a Villa Valguarnera a Bagheria

republika.description: In primo grado la giovane era stata condannata a 9 anni

republika.title: Allarme rientrato per gli astronauti della Stazione spaziale internazionale. Resta la perdita d'aria
republika.description: Individuate due fessure sul modulo russo, da cui fuoriesce circa un chilo d’aria al giorno. Durante le riparazioni, effettuate dai cosmonauti, gli altri cinque membri dell’equipaggio sono entrati nella navicella Dragon, pronti a rientrare sulla Terra

republika.title: Francia, il caso della bimba uccisa dal pedofilo che fa tremare lo Stato: il sospettato era già noto
republika.description: Lyhanna, 11 anni, era scomparsa da una settimana. Ora il ritrovamento del corpo mette sotto accusa il sistema giudiziario: in passato l’uomo, padre di un’amica della vittima, era stata denunciato per lo stupro di una minore ma doveva ancora essere convocato dalla magistratura. Macron: “Inaccettabile”

republika.title: Riforma medici di famiglia, Pd e M5S: “Ennesimo disastro, il governo implode. Schillaci in aula”
republika.description: Affossata dal centrodestra, le reazioni delle opposizioni: “A pagare saranno ancora una volta famiglie e cittadini. Sono al tutti contro tutti sulla pelle degli italiani”

republika.title: Bolelli e Vavassori, che sfortuna. Eliminati in semifinale a Parigi per l’infortunio di Simone
republika.description: La coppia azzurra sconfitta 7-6 6-4 da Granollers e Ceballos. Nel primo set il problema alla caviglia per il bolognese, che da lì in poi ha giocato da fermo

republika.title: Meloni salta il vertice Ue-Balcani: “Rammaricata per il ritardo”. Era alla presentazione di un francobollo
republika.description: La premier annulla all’ultimo la sua partecipazione al summit Ue-Balcani, in cui si discute anche di Ucraina: “Si è protratta la cerimonia dei carabinieri a Reggio Calabria”

republika.title: Travaglio, il caso Minetti e la prova che il giustizialismo è una slot truccata
republika.description: Così funziona la mentalità che intossica il dibattito pubblico: un avviso di garanzia è una condanna, ma nemmeno una sentenza è valida se contraddice le tesi della propaganda

republika.title: Chi erano Dana e Camilla Galli, sorelle morte in un incidente stradale: Livigno, lo sci, la famiglia
republika.description: Le giovani, 14 e 23 anni, sono morte nello scontro avvenuto sulla Orientale Sebina, poco sopra Iseo, la sera di giovedì: stavano tornando a casa

npr.title: Xi Jinping will travel to North Korea next week in first visit since 2019
npr.description: The announcement was made by both countries Friday a day after North Korea unveiled a new facility to produce nuclear fuel.

npr.title: South Africa rolls out game-changing HIV shot amid funding shortfalls
npr.description: A new twice-yearly HIV prevention injection could transform South Africa's fight against the epidemic — but U.S. aid cuts and limited doses threaten to slow its impact.

npr.title: China's highest bridge brings tourists and internet access to remote communities
npr.description: A link to the highway that cuts travel times from hours to just minutes, and a symbol of a flow of investment that has provided unprecedented access to high-speed internet in this remote region.

npr.title: Protesters in Albania oppose plan for Trump family-linked resort
npr.description: Protesters in Albania oppose Jared Kushner's planned Adriatic coast resort, which would be located in one of the Mediterranean's most environmentally sensitive areas.

npr.title: Putin says Russia will bolster air defenses in response to Ukrainian drone attacks
npr.description: President Vladimir Putin says Russia will strengthen its air defenses to counter recent Ukrainian drone attacks, which have reached deep inside his country and cast a cloud over his showcase economic forum in his hometown of St. Petersburg.

npr.title: North Korea unveils a new plant to produce fuel for nuclear weapons
npr.description: State media photos on the place showed it is likely a plant to produce weapons-grade uranium.

npr.title: Hezbollah rejects ceasefire deal agreed on by Israel and Lebanon
npr.description: The U.N. peacekeeping mission for Lebanon, known as UNIFIL, said one peacekeeper was killed and others were wounded when they came under mortar fire in southeastern Lebanon.

npr.title: Russia's economic forum opens against backdrop of Ukrainian strikes
npr.description: The St. Petersburg International Economic Forum -- Russia's answer to Davos -- opens under the shadow of Ukrainian drone attacks and growing economic uncertainty.

npr.title: Peru election could add to string of right-wing victories in Latin America
npr.description: Peruvians go to the polls Sunday to elect their next president amid a conservative shift in Latin America. The daughter of a former dictator, a far-right senator, could win.

npr.title: Plans for a Trump family-linked resort spark protests in Albania
npr.description: A coastal development project linked to Jared Kushner is facing resistance in Albania. The government says the project will transform the nation, but environmental campaigners and critics oppose it.

elpais.title: El Vaticano sale al paso de la polémica con las víctimas de pederastia y confirma que el Papa se reunirá con ellas en España
elpais.description: El periodista británico Gareth Gore afirma que pidió un encuentro del Pontífice con afectados del Opus Dei, pero le han respondido que ya está cerrada una cita con otro grupo de sobrevivientes

elpais.title: Agenda interactiva de la visita del papa León XIV a España por días y ciudades
elpais.description: Siete jornadas, siete localidades, actos inéditos y eventos multitudinarios, una guía para seguir paso a paso el primer viaje de un pontífice al país desde 2011

elpais.title: Sánchez: “Nunca avalé, conocí o permití nada de lo que hacía Leire Díez. Yo no he hecho lo que me hicieron a mí”
elpais.description: El presidente mantiene el apoyo a la directora de la Guardia Civil y asegura que no habrá superdomingo electoral

elpais.title: Qué apuntó Leire Díez en sus cuadernos: contactos, objetivos y “asuntos abiertos”
elpais.description: La exmilitante socialista anotó en una de sus libretas “reunión con P. S.”, pero La Moncloa asegura que Sánchez no ha tenido jamás una reunión ni un encuentro con ella

elpais.title: La UCO espera desde Navidades a que el juez la autorice a investigar a la pareja de Ayuso
elpais.description: El caso de posible soborno a un jefe de Quirón se ha congelado desde que se jubiló la magistrada que lo abrió, que fue sustituida en octubre por Antonio Viejo

elpais.title: Negociación a lo “reality show”: los profesores valencianos llegan al vigésimo día de huelga sin acuerdo
elpais.description: Las concentraciones y protestas en apoyo a los docentes se suceden, como el llamamiento de la confederación de madres y padres Gonzalo Anaya a vaciar las aulas

elpais.title: Los profesores catalanes convocan huelga durante la visita del Papa en Barcelona
elpais.description: Los docentes protagonizan este viernes un nuevo paro, mientras el Govern cierra la puerta a nuevas conversaciones: “El momento de la negociación ha acabado”

elpais.title: Enrique Riquelme anuncia que su apuesta para el banquillo del Real Madrid es Jürgen Klopp
elpais.description: El candidato a la presidencia del Real Madrid comunica que, si gana las elecciones del domingo, Raúl González se pondrá en contacto con el técnico alemán

elpais.title: Enrique Riquelme: “Uno no puede venir a enfrentarse al sistema del Real Madrid con miedo”
elpais.description: El empresario, el primero que reta a Florentino Pérez en las urnas en más de dos décadas, explica en esta entrevista los puntos calientes de la campaña

elpais.title: Todas las selecciones del Mundial 2026 en Estados Unidos, Canadá y México
elpais.description: La competición con más equipos de la historia pone en juego a 48 combinados nacionales durante cinco semanas. Consulte aquí todos los detalles

elpais.title: ¿Es posible morirse de pena? La ciencia confirma que el duelo intenso eleva el riesgo de muerte
elpais.description: La tristeza prolongada por la pérdida de un ser querido casi duplica la probabilidad de fallecer en un plazo de 10 años, aunque es mayor en los seis primeros meses

elpais.title: ‘Manoliño’ y otros delfines que se arriesgan acercándose a las personas para escapar de su soledad
elpais.description: Un estudio documenta cómo estos cetáceos se dejan tocar y juegan, una relación inusual que puede suponer un peligro para su bienestar y el de las personas con las que se relacionan

elpais.description: Maridos neveristas, cuñadas que arruinan ensaladas y niños discriminados porque su madre les envuelve el bocata en papel albal: el consultorio de junio está lleno de dramas familiares

elpais.title: Una fuga de aire en la Estación Espacial Internacional obliga a los astronautas a refugiarse en una nave durante dos horas
elpais.description: Los tripulantes, que se prepararon para una evacuación mientras se revisaba el fallo, ya han podido reingresar en la estación

undark.title: The Six-Week Postpartum Checkup Comes Too Late

This single doctor’s appointment may be efficient for billing and discharge protocols, but the timing reflects the structure of the health care system more than the reality of maternal recovery.

undark.title: Book Review:  The Case for Making Data-Driven Decisions

undark.title: What the Hantavirus Story Reveals About Medical Mistrust

In the U.S., hantavirus disproportionately kills Native Americans. A doctor who works at a hospital on Navajo Nation writes that such mistrust always lands hardest on the most vulnerable.

undark.title: When Scientific Arguments Obscure Moral Ones, Democracy Suffers

undark.title: Book Review: The Life and Struggles of a Conservation Pioneer

In “Homesick for a World Unknown,” Miriam Horn documents his triumphs, challenges, and setbacks in meticulous detail.

proj-syn.title: The ECB Should Not Raise Interest Rates Yet
proj-syn.description: Against a backdrop of acute uncertainty, weak growth, subdued wages, and elevated market interest rates, monetary tightening is warranted only when there is convincing evidence that higher inflation is becoming entrenched. No such evidence has yet materialized in Europe.

proj-syn.title: When Markets Run on Empty
proj-syn.description: Markets are flying high despite geopolitical turmoil because a broad-based willingness to keep spending has been matched by an ability to keep doing so. But as more economic participants exhaust their means and rely on debt, a painful moment of truth will arrive—sooner rather than later if the Strait of Hormuz remains closed.

proj-syn.title: The Pope and the AI Profiteers
proj-syn.description: In his first encyclical, Pope Leo XIV rightly rejects the idea that markets alone can be trusted to shape society’s technological future. Recognizing that AI raises questions that prices and profits cannot answer, the Chicago-born pope has posed a direct challenge to Chicago School economics.

proj-syn.title: AI Must Not Encroach on Human Dignity
proj-syn.description: In a world captivated by technological advances, Pope Leo XIV’s first encyclical seeks to shift attention away from the marvels and terrors of AI and toward the magnificence of humanity. The message that the technology lacks a “moral conscience” and is distinct from human cognition is necessary and welcome.

proj-syn.title: The Key Forces Now Shaping Markets and Geopolitics
proj-syn.description: Three major factors are likely to shape economic and geopolitical outcomes over the next several years: politically unconstrained AI development, a shift from the logic of globalization to zero-sum thinking, and heightened international tail risks. Much could go right, or at least as expected—until it doesn’t.

proj-syn.title: The Living Ghosts of Violent Radicalism
proj-syn.description: Following World War II, the most militant student movements emerged in the former Axis powers as a way to cope with previous generations' complicity. But while the Red Army Faction and others were haunted by memories of past crimes, today's young people have mostly forgotten, and a growing number think far-right politics are cool.

proj-syn.title: Using AI to Test Policy Language
proj-syn.description: Policymakers have long understood that language affects economic behavior, but until recently, there were few tools capable of systematically analyzing its effects. AI may now help close that gap, enabling officials to anticipate how framing and timing can move markets and shift public opinion.

proj-syn.title: Europe’s Competitiveness Bogeyman
proj-syn.description: Calls for European leaders to protect domestic industry from "unfairly" subsidized Chinese competition have lately grown louder. But while tariffs might offer temporary relief to a few sectors, they cannot restore Europe's technological leadership, industrial dynamism, or export competitiveness.

proj-syn.title: Putting American Science on a MAGA Leash
proj-syn.description: A draft rule from US President Donald Trump’s White House Office of Management and Budget would subject all scientific research funding to the whims of political appointees, further undercutting a pillar of American power. The goal is to foreclose any future that is plural, contestable, and beyond the president’s control.

proj-syn.title: How Measles Came Roaring Back
proj-syn.description: Bangladesh is facing soaring measles cases not because of a single localized failure, but because of years of systemic erosion. Ultimately, maintaining herd immunity against highly contagious viruses requires relentless attention to supply and demand, as well as to the broader social and institutional foundations of public health.

proj-syn.title: Pete Hegseth’s Dangerous Call to Arms in Asia
proj-syn.description: Much like it did in Europe, the Trump administration has called on US allies in the Indo-Pacific to increase military spending to 3.5% of GDP. But a defense buildup on this scale would jeopardize economic growth and regional unity, and could lead Southeast Asian countries to gravitate toward China’s strategic orbit.

proj-syn.title: The Pope’s AI Vision and Its Limits
proj-syn.description: Pope Leo XIV’s encyclical on AI is clear-eyed about the limits of techno-utopianism. But its vision of technology directed toward human flourishing needs to be extended to include the interests of every sentient being, human and nonhuman, biological or—possibly—artificial.

proj-syn.title: The Iran War Is Fueling a Global Debt Shock
proj-syn.description: Once again, a global crisis is disproportionately burdening countries that did not cause it. Across the Global South, the food- and energy-price shock triggered by the conflict in the Middle East has morphed into a debt shock that demands an urgent international response.

proj-syn.title: Democracy vs. Data Centers
proj-syn.description: As tech companies race to build data centers, communities and lawmakers across the United States are pushing back. Industry leaders frame local opposition as a threat to American competitiveness, but China’s experience shows that unchecked expansion carries serious risks of its own.

proj-syn.title: The Right Incentives for Climate Action
proj-syn.description: As the closure of the Strait of Hormuz continues to disrupt global oil and gas flows, countries are increasingly focusing on short-term energy priorities to the detriment of long-term decarbonization goals. In such a context, the difficult task of designing climate policies that realign incentives takes on new importance.

proj-syn.title: The US and India Have Become Regional Rivals
proj-syn.description: While the US views India as a counterweight to China in Asia, it balks at the idea of Indian regional dominance, preferring a pluralistic order. The Trump administration has gone further by pursuing close ties with Pakistan, apparently hoping that the US and India can remain global partners.

proj-syn.title: Digital Sovereignty Is in the Fine Print
proj-syn.description: Despite efforts to build their own digital industries and infrastructure, most countries remain dependent on American tech firms for the provision of core government services. But government officials can tip the balance of bargaining power by attaching certain standardized provisions to public procurement and services contracts.

proj-syn.title: Trump Wants to Privatize His Presidential Records
proj-syn.description: By enacting the Presidential Records Act in response to Richard Nixon’s malfeasance, the US Congress created a process to limit abuse of power and ensure accountability. Like Nixon, Donald Trump seems determined to avoid accountability, which has led his Justice Department to argue—poorly—that the PRA is unconstitutional.
